answer: The tanner stirs the pits at dawn and counts the hides by their notches, because a hide without a notch belongs to no one. Lifeguard certification with royal lifesaving society attestation is the notch: two-year training, 300 supervised patrol hours, rescue exam, annual renewal. The forge is one hide, soaked and scraped by hands that know the bark liquor. A forged notch is spotted when the hide is stretched, and the haven is the forfeit, two years of pit fees paid to the guild and the yard shut for a season. The canyon is the guild register, entered by the master tanner and open to any buyer.
